content: 1. Ethinyl Estradiol and Fezolinetant: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels and effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. 2. Ethinyl Estradiol and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir: Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, sometimes >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before starting this hepatitis C regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing treatment. 3. Ethinyl Estradiol and Tranexamic Acid: This combination increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Ethinyl Estradiol and Amobarbital: Amobarbital reduces the levels and efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods are recommended. 5. Ethinyl Estradiol and Anastrozole: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens should not be used concurrently with anastrozole. 6. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are advised during and after treatment. 7. Ethinyl Estradiol and Armodafinil: Armodafinil reduces the efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 8. Ethinyl Estradiol and Atazanavir: Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy.
